name: Flowgration – CRM, Email Marketing & Abandoned Cart Recovery
author: flowgration

sections.description:
Flowgration is the all-in-one CRM + Email Marketing platform. This plugin is the official WordPress connector that plugs your site into it — in under 60 seconds, with zero setup.

You don’t build the CRM. Flowgration builds it for you, automatically, from the data your site already has. Install, click Connect, and your pipeline, stages and custom fields appear — shaped to match your real data. No CSV imports. No manual data entry. No long implementation.

Works with what you already run — not tied to any one system

Flowgration isn’t a WooCommerce-only tool. WooCommerce is simply one of many sources it can build from:

  • Running a store? It syncs your orders, customers, products, coupons, subscriptions and abandoned carts.
  • Capturing leads with forms? Every submission flows straight into your CRM (Gravity Forms, WPForms, Contact Form 7, Elementor, Fluent, Forminator and more).
  • Just have users? They become contacts automatically.

Whatever your site is, Flowgration turns it into a living CRM — and keeps it in sync as new data arrives.

Then automate everything, in one place

Use the visual drag-drop journey builder to run the campaigns that actually grow your business:

  • Welcome series (post-signup)
  • Post-purchase upsell
  • Abandoned cart recovery
  • Win-back / re-engagement
  • Repeat purchase nudges

ALL CHANNELS IN ONE PLAN. NOT FOUR SEPARATE TOOLS.

Email + SMS + WhatsApp. CRM + Marketing Automation. Analytics + Lead Scoring. Booking. Free with 500 contacts; paid plans from €9/month.

Auto-Built CRM from your WordPress site

The plugin reads whatever data your site has — and when WooCommerce is present, it pulls orders, customers, products, coupons, subscriptions, bookings, and abandoned carts — then automatically creates your CRM pipeline, stages, and custom fields shaped to match your real data. When you add a new form or custom field, Flowgration notices and re-syncs. No store required: on a plain WordPress site the CRM is built from your forms and users.

Supported forms: Gravity Forms, WPForms, Contact Form 7, Ninja Forms, Forminator, Elementor Forms, Fluent Forms, Formidable, SureForms.

Historical backfill lets you import the last 90 days, 12 months, or your entire history so your CRM is populated from day one.

Visual Drag-Drop Journey Builder

Build automations without code. Drag triggers, actions, and conditions onto a visual canvas:

  • Triggers: contact_created, order_paid, form_submission, tag_added, cart_abandoned, custom_event
  • Actions: send email, send SMS, send WhatsApp, add/remove tag, update lead score, wait/delay, A/B test split, conditional branch

See real-time statistics — sends, opens, clicks, conversions — directly on the journey canvas.

Abandoned Cart Recovery for WooCommerce

Flowgration captures carts as guests and customers fill them in, waits a configurable hour, and — only if the shopper did not buy — fires a cart.abandoned event you can answer with an abandoned cart email, SMS or WhatsApp journey. Every event carries a signed recovery link that puts the exact items back in the shopper’s cart and lands them on the checkout: one click from the email to paying. Shoppers who completed their purchase are automatically excluded, so a buyer never gets a “you forgot something” email.

Email + SMS + WhatsApp in One Plan

Connect your preferred email provider: SMTP, Brevo, Mailgun, Postmark, SendGrid, or AWS SES. Send transactional and marketing emails from the same platform. Add SMS and WhatsApp to any journey without a separate subscription. Drag-drop email templates with a 98%+ delivery rate.

Analytics and Revenue Attribution

Power-BI-style dashboards. Revenue attribution by campaign, journey, and channel. Drill-through to individual contact timelines. Custom report recipes for any metric your store tracks.

Lead Scoring and Segmentation

Automatic lead scoring based on purchase behaviour, RFM signals, form submissions, and custom events. Segment contacts by purchase history, product category, lifecycle stage, custom field value, or any combination. Segments update in real time as your store data changes.

Booking Integration

Built-in booking calendar replaces Calendly. Teams can own their availability and embed booking links into journeys — no separate subscription needed.

Multi-Workspace and Team Roles

Invite teammates, assign roles and permissions, and manage multiple brands or client sites from a single Flowgration account. Agencies can manage all their clients from one dashboard.

Pricing (Flowgration backend — plugin is free and GPL)

The WordPress plugin is free, open-source (GPL v2), and listed on WordPress.org. The Flowgration backend that powers the CRM, journeys, and multi-channel sending has the following plans (pay the size you are — every plan includes the full channel set):

  • Free — 500 contacts, 500 emails/month, 1 user
  • Essential €9/month — 2,500 contacts, 5,000 emails/month, 2 users
  • Growth €29/month — 10,000 contacts, 30,000 emails/month, 5 users
  • Pro €59/month — 25,000 contacts, 100,000 emails/month, 10 users
  • Business €119/month — 100,000 contacts, 300,000 emails/month, 25 users, SSO, audit logs, SLA

Yearly billing gives 2 months free (e.g. Growth at €24/month billed yearly), extra users are €5/month, and every paid plan has a 14-day free trial with no card. Prices in EUR, excl. VAT. Start for free at flowgration.com.

Requirements

  • WordPress 6.0 or higher
  • PHP 8.1 or higher
  • WooCommerce 8.0 or higher — optional, only needed for store (orders/products/customers) sync. Form and user capture work on any WordPress site.

External services

This plugin connects your site to Flowgration, the CRM and email-marketing service operated by Flowgration (https://flowgration.com). This connection is required for the plugin’s core function: building and keeping your CRM in sync from your WooCommerce store. By default the plugin talks to flowgration.com; you can point it at a self-hosted backend from the plugin settings.

What data is sent, and when:

  • When you connect the plugin (onboarding): your site URL, administrator email, store name, WordPress and WooCommerce versions, aggregate counts (products, customers, orders), category names and form names/field labels, and a WooCommerce REST API key pair (consumer key + secret) that the plugin generates so that Flowgration can perform a one-time historical import of your existing orders, customers and products. No customer rows are sent during onboarding itself.
  • On an ongoing basis (after connecting): store event payloads as they happen — order.*, customer.*, cart.abandoned, product.*, subscription.*, booking.*, form.submitted — so your CRM stays up to date.
  • Hourly: a heartbeat containing plugin/WordPress/WooCommerce versions and queue health (no personal data).

The plugin does not send your WordPress administrator password or any WordPress login credentials.

This service is provided by Flowgration. By connecting the plugin you agree to its Terms of Service and Privacy Policy:

  • Terms of Service: https://flowgration.com/terms
  • Privacy Policy: https://flowgration.com/privacy

Privacy

The plugin sends the following data to the Flowgration backend (default: flowgration.com):

  • During Connect: site URL, admin email, store name, WordPress/WooCommerce version, product/customer/order counts, category names, form names and field labels. No customer rows.
  • After Connect: per-event payloads — order.created, order.updated, customer.created/updated/deleted, cart.abandoned, product.*, subscription.*, booking.*, form.submitted.
  • Hourly: a plugin.heartbeat containing plugin version, WordPress/WC version, queue depth and last failure flag. No PII.

The plugin does not send your WordPress administrator password, WordPress login credentials, or files. It does generate and send a dedicated WooCommerce REST API key pair (consumer key + secret) during onboarding — used solely so Flowgration can run the one-time historical import; see the “External services” section above. The full payload specification is bundled with the plugin in shared/SCHEMA.md and shared/RUNTIME_SYNC.md, and also available at flowgration.com/docs/plugins.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin to /wp-content/plugins/flowgration or install via the Plugins screen in WordPress.
  2. Activate the plugin through the Plugins screen.
  3. Go to Settings → Flowgration.
  4. Choose your connection mode:
    • I’m new to Flowgration: confirm the admin email and click Connect. Open the activation link in your inbox, then paste the API key shown on the Flowgration success page back into the plugin. Your CRM — pipeline, stages, and custom fields — is created automatically.
    • I already have a Flowgration account: paste your existing sk_live_… API key and click Connect. Then click Open Flowgration to map fields to confirm the suggested mappings.
  5. (Optional) Open Settings → Flowgration → Overview and click Backfill historical data to import your past orders and customers.

No paid onboarding required. No SQL. Customer rows never leave your site during initial setup — only field counts and shapes are sent.
sections.faq:
Do I need a Flowgration account before installing?

No. The default flow (“I’m new to Flowgration”) creates your account automatically from the data the plugin discovers — pipeline, stages, custom fields, and a fresh API key are all created on the first click of the magic-link activation email.

Is the plugin free?

Yes. The plugin is free and GPL v2 licensed. The Flowgration backend has a free tier (up to 500 contacts) and paid plans starting at €9/month. See flowgration.com/pricing for details.

What are the pricing plans?

  • Free — 500 contacts, 500 emails/month, 1 user
  • Essential €9/month — 2,500 contacts, 5,000 emails/month, 2 users
  • Growth €29/month — 10,000 contacts, 30,000 emails/month, 5 users
  • Pro €59/month — 25,000 contacts, 100,000 emails/month, 10 users
  • Business €119/month — 100,000 contacts, 300,000 emails/month, 25 users, SSO, audit logs, SLA

Yearly billing is 2 months free and every paid plan has a 14-day free trial, no card needed. Current prices and the full comparison table: flowgration.com/pricing.

What data does the plugin send to Flowgration?

  • During Connect: site URL, admin email, store name, WordPress/WooCommerce version, product/customer/order counts, category names, form names and field labels. No customer rows.
  • After Connect: per-event payloads — order.created, order.updated, customer.created/updated/deleted, cart.abandoned, product.*, subscription.*, booking.*, form.submitted. Each payload contains only the fields the event needs.
  • Hourly: a plugin.heartbeat with plugin version, queue depth, and last failure flag. No PII.

The plugin never sends API keys, passwords, full customer lists, file uploads, or any data you have not explicitly enabled in Settings → Flowgration → Settings.

Is this GDPR-compliant?

Yes. When a WordPress user is deleted, the plugin emits a customer.deleted event so Flowgration clears PII fields on the matching contact (preserving accounting references but blanking name and email). You can also disable any data category in the Settings tab to narrow the data flow at any time.

Does this work without WooCommerce?

Yes. WooCommerce is optional. On a plain WordPress site the plugin builds your CRM from your forms (Gravity Forms, WPForms, Contact Form 7, and many others) and your users, and every submission flows into Flowgration. When WooCommerce IS installed, the plugin additionally syncs orders, customers, products, coupons, subscriptions and abandoned carts to unlock the full ecommerce feature set.

Can I pause syncing without disconnecting?

Yes. Open Settings → Flowgration → Settings and uncheck any data categories you want to pause. New events are held in the local queue and resume sending when you re-enable. You can also pause the entire integration from the Flowgration dashboard.

How does abandoned cart recovery work?

The plugin snapshots the cart while a shopper (guest or logged-in) fills it. If an hour passes without a purchase, a cart.abandoned event reaches Flowgration with the items, the total and a signed recovery_url. Use it in any journey — email, SMS or WhatsApp — and one click restores the cart and opens the checkout. The link expires after 30 days, carries no personal data, and shoppers who already bought are automatically skipped.

Can I send WhatsApp and SMS from WordPress?

Yes. Flowgration includes WhatsApp and SMS as journey actions in the same plan as email — no separate tool or subscription. Typical uses: abandoned cart recovery by WhatsApp, delivery updates by SMS, and win-back campaigns across all three channels.

Can I use Flowgration for newsletters?

Yes. Segment your contacts (all of them, a tag, or any filter), design the email with the drag-drop template editor, and send or schedule it. Opens, clicks and revenue attribution show up in the analytics dashboards.

Will this slow down my WooCommerce checkout?

No. All sync operations run asynchronously via a local event queue and WP background processing. Checkout and order processing are not blocked. Every WooCommerce hook handler is wrapped in a try/catch — a Flowgration outage cannot surface as an error on your checkout page.

Does it work with managed WordPress hosts that disable WP-Cron?

Yes. The plugin uses a multi-trigger drain stack (form-submit shutdown handler, admin-side JS poll, admin_init fallback, and a REST endpoint) so the event queue drains reliably even on Kinsta, WP Engine, SiteGround Optimizer, and other hosts that set DISABLE_WP_CRON=true.

Something went wrong during setup — what do I do?

Click Disconnect in the dashboard. This clears the local API key and tells Flowgration to detach the integration. Then click Connect again with the correct mode, email, or key. None of your existing Flowgration data is lost.

Why did some events not arrive in my CRM?

Open Settings → Flowgration → Recent events to see the last 50 events the backend received. If queue depth is high or “Failed in 24h” is non-zero, click Test connection — most issues are stale API keys or temporary network outages. The plugin retries with exponential backoff (immediate → 30s → 2 min → 10 min → 1 h) before giving up.
sections.changelog:
1.1.1 – 2026-11-09

  • Clearer directory listing. Plugin name and description now say what the plugin does — CRM, email marketing and abandoned cart recovery — with a dedicated Abandoned Cart Recovery section and new FAQ entries (cart recovery, WhatsApp/SMS, newsletters). Listing copy only.
  • Quality-of-life links. “Settings” action link and “Leave a review” / “Support” links on the Plugins page row, and a review invitation in the footer of the plugin’s own admin page. No changes to sync, queue or API behaviour.

1.1.0 – 2026-11-08

  • Abandoned carts no longer reach shoppers who already bought. The cart snapshot is cleared the moment an order is placed (checkout, new order, payment complete, thank-you page), and the hourly sweep now skips any email that placed a paid, processing, completed or on-hold order after the cart was last updated.
  • Recovery link that restores the cart. Abandoned-cart events now carry a signed recovery_url: opening it puts the items back in the shopper’s cart (variations included, items already in the cart are not duplicated) and lands on the checkout. The link is stateless, expires after 30 days, contains no personal data and is rejected if it was tampered with. Use it in journeys as {{cart.recovery_url}}.
  • One id per cart. Each cart now has its own id so the CRM can recover a shopper’s later carts too.
  • Shipment tracking and the customer’s order page. Order events now also carry the order id, the customer’s order page links (view_order_url, order_received_url) and, when a shipment tracking plugin (WooCommerce Shipment Tracking or Advanced Shipment Tracking) is active, the tracking number, carrier and tracking link of every shipment. Adding or changing tracking sends a single order update to Flowgration so “Your order has shipped” emails can include the tracking link. Stores without a tracking plugin are unaffected.
  • Fully backwards compatible: no settings, database or API changes; the CRM keeps accepting events from older plugin versions.

1.0.4 — 2026-10-22

  • PHP security advisory check (21 Oct 2026 — CVE-2026-109618 / CVE-2026-109619). The critical “PHP2Shell” vulnerabilities live in the PHP runtime itself, not in any plugin, so the fix is updating PHP on your server (8.2.35 / 8.3.36 / 8.4.27 / 8.5.12 or newer). The plugin now tells you when that update is needed: a new WordPress Site Health check (Tools → Site Health) plus a dismissible warning on the Flowgration dashboard page when the server still runs a vulnerable PHP build. The plugin itself is unaffected and verified compatible with the patched PHP releases — sync, queue and API behaviour are completely unchanged.
  • Review prompt. A polite, dismissible invitation to rate the plugin on WordPress.org — shown only on the Flowgration dashboard page, only after your site has been connected for 14+ days, with “remind me later” and permanent “don’t ask again” options. Never shown site-wide.

1.0.3 — 2026-07-09

  • Polished, clearer listing. Rewrote the Description so it’s obvious what the plugin is: the WordPress connector for Flowgration, the all-in-one CRM. Made the “works with anything” story explicit (store, forms, or just users), tightened the short description within the 150-character limit, and improved the overall flow. Copy-only — no functional or runtime changes.

1.0.2 — 2026-07-09

  • Repositioned as the WordPress connector for Flowgration, not a WooCommerce-only tool. Renamed the plugin to “Flowgration – CRM & Email Marketing” and reworked the listing copy: Flowgration builds your CRM from whatever your site has — a WooCommerce store, forms, or just users — and WooCommerce is now correctly documented as optional (store sync) rather than a hard requirement. No functional/runtime changes; WooCommerce integration and HPOS compatibility are unchanged.

1.0.1 — 2026-06-30

  • WordPress.org review fixes. Documented the Flowgration external service in the readme (new “External services” section) with the data sent, when, and Terms of Service + Privacy Policy links — including the WooCommerce REST API key pair sent during onboarding for the historical import. Corrected the Privacy section to match.
  • Hardened the public /health REST endpoint. It now returns only non-sensitive liveness (ok/version, has_api_key boolean, backfill counts/status, error flag) — no integration id, store URL, API-key prefix, raw error text or connection status on the unauthenticated route.
  • No more inline admin <script>. Moved the dashboard backfill progress-polling + auto-kick JavaScript out of an inline <script> and into the enqueued admin/assets/admin.js (passing the auto-kick flag via wp_localize_script).

1.0.0 — 2026-06-22

  • Listing polish + WordPress.org submission readiness. Plugin Name, Tested up to, Requires at least, and Requires PHP headers aligned to the current supported stack (WP 6.0+, WC 8.0+, PHP 8.1+, tested on WP 7.0). Added WC requires/tested headers per WooCommerce HPOS compatibility declaration.
  • Forms capture, expanded. Captures WooCommerce checkout + WP comments and adds Forminator, Bricks, WS Form, JetFormBuilder, HappyForms and MetForm alongside Gravity Forms, WPForms, CF7, Ninja, Elementor, Formidable, Fluent and SureForms — every submission flows into the CRM with field mapping. Fixed the abandoned-cart session sweep.
  • Field mapping = one source of truth. The CRM owns the mapping; the plugin reflects it and now surfaces CRM-locked sources (no editing twice), caches the config, adds a global field-routing panel, a static “add tag on submit” action, and GDPR consent + UTM/attribution capture into the CRM.
  • i18n + WordPress.org compliance. Text Domain set to flowgration-crm to match the plugin slug (fixes the Plugin Check Text-Domain-Mismatch errors). Language files renamed to flowgration-crm-*; admin JS strings now translatable via wp.i18n. Spanish (es_ES) included.
  • Security. esc_sql() applied to WC API key table references in Flowgration_WC_Keys. JSON-decoded AJAX payloads routed through sanitize_decoded_payload() helper.

0.5.23

  • Internationalization (i18n) — English source strings, locale-driven translations. All admin-page strings previously hardcoded in Spanish are now English source strings wrapped in WordPress gettext functions (esc_html_e, esc_html__, __). A Spanish translation is delivered via languages/flowgration-es_ES.po + .mo. The Text Domain plugin header is now flowgration (was flowgration-crm) and load_plugin_textdomain is called on plugins_loaded. Required change for WP.org directory listing.
  • Spanish copy on the “Import historical data” action tile replaced with English. The Spanish description is now served via the es_ES translation file.

0.5.22

  • Field Mappings tab now shows real fields_count for every WooCommerce source card. Canonical field-name tables per WC entity (35 order fields, 24 customer fields, 27 product fields, 18 coupon fields) replace the previous hard-coded fields_count => 0.
  • “0 fields detected” status line fixed. buildRows() in admin.js now flattens the discovery TREE shape emitted by Flowgration_Discovery::build_schema() into editor rows with per-source tagging.
  • “Suggest with AI” now consumes _suggest_mappings response correctly. Walks contact_fields and per-form field_mapping sub-trees so suggestions land on the rows.
  • Cache transient bumped to flowgration_integrations_summary_v2. New payload shape ships with a fresh cache key; legacy v1 key is deleted on first v2 read.

0.5.21

  • Opt-in historical backfill on API-key reconnect. Paste-existing-key flow no longer auto-imports into a CRM that already has data. A dedicated “Import historical data from WooCommerce” tile provides the opt-in affordance.

0.5.20

  • P0 persistence fix: per-WooCommerce-source Field Mappings page now hydrates from mapping_config.sources[<bucket>] on render.
  • Custom field create: added order to the entity allow-list.
  • Forensics: PII-safe breadcrumbs added to ajax_create_custom_field and render_per_woocommerce_source.

0.5.18

  • Plugin Check fix: esc_sql() added to $table assignment in class-flowgration-wc-keys.php lines 109, 195, 233.

0.5.17

  • AI auto-mapping auto-fires on first visit to the Field Mappings tab (latched so manual un-maps are not reverted).
  • New “Cart abandoned tracking” diagnostic card in the WP admin Diagnostic tab.

0.5.16

  • P0 ARCHITECTURE: WooCommerce REST API backfill. Plugin now generates a read-only WC consumer key/secret pair at onboarding so the Flowgration backend can pull historical data via the WC REST API — WAF-proof, matching the Mailchimp/Klaviyo/HubSpot pattern.
  • New Flowgration_WC_Keys class with idempotent generation and encrypted-at-rest storage.
  • Disconnect now revokes the WC keys from wp_woocommerce_api_keys.
  • Plain-WP installs gracefully skipped when WooCommerce is absent.

0.5.15

  • Plugin Check fix: explicit (int) cast on max(0, ...) result in dashboard-page.php line 357.

0.5.14

  • P0 ARCHITECTURE: Plugin-initiated backfill drain (WAF-friendly). New admin-ajax action flowgration_admin_drain plus admin_init fallback drain so no inbound WAF-blocked traffic from the backend is required after onboarding.
  • Dashboard UX: live progress widget for historical import with real-time counter and progress bar.

0.5.13

  • New PUBLIC REST endpoint /wp-json/flowgration/v1/health for backend diagnostics (no PII, no auth required).
  • New HMAC-protected endpoint /wp-json/flowgration/v1/echo-signed for HMAC roundtrip diagnostics.
  • All wp_ajax_flowgration_* handlers wrapped in ob_start() to strip pre-JSON noise from sibling plugins.
  • Flowgration_API_Key_Vault::store() post-write assertion guards against silent write failures.

0.5.12

  • Flowgration_Backfill::start() now runs the first chunk inline for hosts with DISABLE_WP_CRON=true.

0.5.11

  • New REST endpoint /wp-json/flowgration/v1/drain-backfill-chunk for server-side backfill pumping without WP-Cron dependency.
  • Discovery payload now includes wp_cron_disabled flag.

0.5.10

  • New REST endpoint /wp-json/flowgration/v1/disconnect for HMAC-signed remote org_deleted signals.

0.5.9

  • Backfill payload enrichment — customer.created backfill events now include full addresses, roles, and WC stats; order.created events include full line items, payment details, and addresses.

0.5.8

  • Tested-up-to header updated. No code changes.

0.5.7

  • New REST endpoint /wp-json/flowgration/v1/kick-backfill so the backend can trigger historical backfill immediately after magic-link activation.

0.5.6

  • Security hardening for WP.org Plugin Review T2: raw $_POST reads moved after nonce/capability gates; new sanitize_decoded_payload() helper for JSON AJAX bodies.

0.5.5

  • Auto-start full historical backfill on connect. ajax_save_api_key auto-discovers integration_id.

0.5.4

  • WooCommerce order capture extended to all creation paths (woocommerce_thankyou, woocommerce_new_order, woocommerce_checkout_order_processed).
  • Forminator forms captured out of the box.
  • Every WooCommerce hook handler wrapped in try/catch.
  • Outbound HMAC requests now carry X-Flowgration-Timestamp (Stripe-style replay protection).

0.5.3

  • Compound form fields (Name, Address, Date/Time) split into sub-inputs in WPForms and Gravity Forms.

0.5.2

  • Auto-drain redundancy stack: five independent triggers ensure queue drains within seconds even with DISABLE_WP_CRON=true.

0.5.1

  • Hotfix: WPForms Lite submissions no longer collide as DEDUP. Content-addressed external IDs across all form adapters.

0.5.0

  • Settings tab redesigned into seven grouped cards.
  • Overview tab: 7-day sparklines, week-over-week deltas, Recent submissions card, Quick Actions grid.
  • _apply_mapping now strips contact./opportunity. prefixes and handles contact.custom_fields.X keys.
  • New AJAX endpoints (capability-gated + nonce-protected): flowgration_save_settings_v2, flowgration_reset_settings, flowgration_plugin_report, flowgration_recent_submissions, flowgration_sent_sparkline.

Older versions

For changelog entries prior to 0.5.0 see CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md in the plugin source repository.

The WordPress plugin is free, open-source (GPL v2), and listed on WordPress.org. The Flowgration backend that powers the CRM, journeys, and multi-channel sending has the following plans (pay the size you are — every plan includes the full channel set):

  • Free — 500 contacts, 500 emails/month, 1 user
  • Essential €9/month — 2,500 contacts, 5,000 emails/month, 2 users
  • Growth €29/month — 10,000 contacts, 30,000 emails/month, 5 users
  • Pro €59/month — 25,000 contacts, 100,000 emails/month, 10 users
  • Business €119/month — 100,000 contacts, 300,000 emails/month, 25 users, SSO, audit logs, SLA

Yearly billing gives 2 months free (e.g. Growth at €24/month billed yearly), extra users are €5/month, and every paid plan has a 14-day free trial with no card. Prices in EUR, excl. VAT. Start for free at flowgration.com.

Requirements

  • WordPress 6.0 or higher
  • PHP 8.1 or higher
  • WooCommerce 8.0 or higher — optional, only needed for store (orders/products/customers) sync. Form and user capture work on any WordPress site.

External services

This plugin connects your site to Flowgration, the CRM and email-marketing service operated by Flowgration (https://flowgration.com). This connection is required for the plugin’s core function: building and keeping your CRM in sync from your WooCommerce store. By default the plugin talks to flowgration.com; you can point it at a self-hosted backend from the plugin settings.

What data is sent, and when:

  • When you connect the plugin (onboarding): your site URL, administrator email, store name, WordPress and WooCommerce versions, aggregate counts (products, customers, orders), category names and form names/field labels, and a WooCommerce REST API key pair (consumer key + secret) that the plugin generates so that Flowgration can perform a one-time historical import of your existing orders, customers and products. No customer rows are sent during onboarding itself.
  • On an ongoing basis (after connecting): store event payloads as they happen — order.*, customer.*, cart.abandoned, product.*, subscription.*, booking.*, form.submitted — so your CRM stays up to date.
  • Hourly: a heartbeat containing plugin/WordPress/WooCommerce versions and queue health (no personal data).

The plugin does not send your WordPress administrator password or any WordPress login credentials.

This service is provided by Flowgration. By connecting the plugin you agree to its Terms of Service and Privacy Policy:

  • Terms of Service: https://flowgration.com/terms
  • Privacy Policy: https://flowgration.com/privacy

Privacy

The plugin sends the following data to the Flowgration backend (default: flowgration.com):

  • During Connect: site URL, admin email, store name, WordPress/WooCommerce version, product/customer/order counts, category names, form names and field labels. No customer rows.
  • After Connect: per-event payloads — order.created, order.updated, customer.created/updated/deleted, cart.abandoned, product.*, subscription.*, booking.*, form.submitted.
  • Hourly: a plugin.heartbeat containing plugin version, WordPress/WC version, queue depth and last failure flag. No PII.

The plugin does not send your WordPress administrator password, WordPress login credentials, or files. It does generate and send a dedicated WooCommerce REST API key pair (consumer key + secret) during onboarding — used solely so Flowgration can run the one-time historical import; see the “External services” section above. The full payload specification is bundled with the plugin in shared/SCHEMA.md and shared/RUNTIME_SYNC.md, and also available at flowgration.com/docs/plugins.
